site.title: Sound & State — Greater Seattle News Reader
site.description: Read articles from Greater Seattle news publications and local Bluesky posts. Browse the curated feed list and save items in your browser.

about.purpose: Sound & State brings together articles from Greater Seattle publications and posts from local accounts so you can follow familiar sources and discover new ones.
about.hosting: GitHub Pages hosts this reader. Cloudflare runs the feed service. Both receive your IP address and request information when your browser contacts them.
about.serviceDetails: The maintainer disables stored request logs and tracing for the feed service. The service uses your IP address to limit repeated requests. Cloudflare and GitHub may still keep service and security records under their own policies. These settings do not guarantee that those companies retain no information about your visits.
about.delivery: Your browser loads feeds through Cloudflare. If Cloudflare cannot get a feed from the publisher, it tries a previously saved copy, when one is available. If Cloudflare still cannot provide the feed, your browser tries to load it directly from the publisher.
about.cache: Cloudflare keeps copies of feeds for up to 15 minutes so it can reuse them across requests. It keeps them for less time when the publisher requires it, and it does not store error responses or content the publisher marks as private.
about.snapshots: GitHub also runs a scheduled task to collect backup copies of the KING 5, KREM 2, and MyNorthwest feeds. The task runs every 15 minutes, though GitHub may delay it. Cloudflare stops using each backup within 6 hours, or sooner if the publisher requires it. Browse publications to see when the task collected a copy. The task does not send your information to publishers.

help.addressPrivacy: When this reader loads a feed, your browser does not save any cookies the publisher sends. The reader keeps track of which items you have read in this browser and never sends that information to a server. When you search or change views, the reader puts your selection after the {hash} in the page address. Your browser does not send that part of the address to the site host.
help.archive: Choose Find archived page to send the article address to Ghostarchive and look for a saved copy. Your browser does not send the address of this reader. The reader first removes tracking parameters whose names start with {prefix}. Ghostarchive may not have a copy.
help.externalArchiveLinks: Publisher and archive links open in a new tab. Those sites apply their own privacy policies and may use cookies.
help.externalPublisherLinks: Publisher links open in a new tab. Those sites apply their own privacy policies and may use cookies.
help.cookies: The reader does not set or read cookies, use analytics, or load fonts from other sites.
help.browserLibrary: The reader keeps saved items, which items you have read, and preferences in this browser. It does not upload them or sync them between devices.
help.clearingStorage: Clearing this site's browser data deletes your library and preferences. If browser storage is unavailable, you lose changes when you close or reload the page.
help.hosting: The website host receives your IP address and page request when you open this reader.
help.serviceRequests: The feed service receives your IP address and the feed you request. If it cannot deliver a feed, your browser may request it directly from the publisher. The publisher then receives your IP address and feed request.
help.directRequests: Your browser requests feeds directly from their publishers. Each publisher receives your IP address and feed request.
help.requestPrivacy: Feed requests send no cookies, login credentials, or address of the page you are viewing.
help.connectionsHeading: How the reader connects and displays content
help.serviceDelivery: Your browser asks the feed service for each curated source. If that request fails, your browser tries to load the feed directly from its publisher.
help.directDelivery: Your browser loads each curated feed directly from its publisher.
help.cors: For that direct attempt to work, the publisher must allow other websites, including this reader, to read its feed in a browser. This permission is called cross-origin resource sharing (CORS). Without it, your browser blocks the reader from accessing the feed.
help.sanitization: The reader removes scripts, embedded pages, forms, and images from feed previews before showing them. Your browser also limits which scripts the reader can run and which sites it can contact.
help.publisherLinks: When you follow a publisher link, your browser does not send the address of this reader to that site.
help.refreshHeading: How the reader refreshes and stores items
help.refreshPolicy: While you view Articles or Posts, the reader checks the feeds that match your filters. It pauses those checks when you leave the tab and checks again when you return. After a feed loads successfully, the reader waits at least 15 minutes before checking it again. If a feed fails, the reader waits longer between attempts. Choose Refresh to retry failed feeds immediately.
help.timeouts: The reader waits up to 15 seconds for each feed, including any direct retry at the publisher. If a feed takes too long, the reader stops waiting and keeps its stored items available. Choose Refresh to try again.
help.newItems: When the reader finds new items while you are reading, it shows their count alongside feed progress in the header. The button stays disabled while feeds are still being checked. Choose Show new articles or Show new posts to add the items, close the status panel, and return to the top of the list.
help.progress: The reader checks your browser’s stored feeds before showing a progress bar. The bar counts completed checks, including feeds the reader could not load. It does not estimate how much time remains. If there are no new items, choose Dismiss feed status to close the finished panel.
help.retention: The reader keeps unsaved items for up to 30 days and up to 150 items per feed. It keeps saved items until you remove them or clear this site's browser data.
help.offline: The reader keeps a copy of the feed list in your browser so you can still browse your library if it cannot download the latest list. You need an internet connection to load new content, and the reader may not reopen while you are offline.
help.scrollRead: The reader starts in Unread and marks articles as read when their titles pass behind the header. For posts, it waits until the post text passes behind the header. Turn off Mark items read as I scroll past them in Reading options if you prefer to mark them yourself. The reader remembers your choice and whether you last selected Latest or Unread.
help.unreadRetention: Items stay in the Unread list after you open them or mark them as read. Choose Unread again, Refresh, or Show new articles or posts to rebuild the list. Changing views, filters, or search also rebuilds it.
help.appearance: Choose Auto, Light, or Dark in the Theme menu. Auto follows your device’s appearance. Select a publisher’s name to see its details and exclude that source from your feeds. Open Excluded sources in the menu to include it again. Saved items remain available, and you can still browse an excluded source directly.
help.swipePreview: On mobile, swipe down from an article preview’s top bar to close it. You can also swipe down from the article content when it is already at the top, or choose Close story.
help.backups: Choose Export reading backup to download a JSON file with your saved articles and posts and a record of which items you have read. Choose Restore backup to add items from a backup and combine its read and saved marks with your current library. Restore backup accepts backups from this collection. You can also choose Export saved items as CSV on the Saved page to download all your saved items for a spreadsheet.
